result:
Round 99 is planned and the decision is **CONTINUE**. The new task fixes a bug I reproduced myself in real Chromium: holding Enter adds one clip for every key auto-repeat instead of one clip per press. Nothing in `store/` changed (`git status` is empty, all 528 frozen files match).

**Round 98 result:** C passed it with real browser checks (`browserVerified=true`), and gate 98 published it as `736db33` on both remotes. That commit is the round 99 baseline. In the backlog I closed GATE97-S1 (the held Enter that reopened the export dialog) and GATE97-S3 (the doc 085 status line) on that evidence.

**C's one finding (C-R98-B1) is closed by decision, with no code change.** Space on the focused toolbar Export button starts or stops playback instead of opening the dialog. That is the long-standing global play/stop shortcut, which the shortcut footer documents. Enter and a mouse click still open Export. The mistake was mine: the round 98 task claimed "Space also opens it, as now" without any earlier test showing it. Future tasks only claim behaviour C has already seen. I made no claim about Ableton (no source consulted).

**Why this bug goes next:** the gate 98 reviewer suspected that in Safari a held Enter could reach the global Enter shortcut, which ignores key repeat. I ran a read-only Playwright probe (`b-round-98-probe/`). Holding Enter went from 0 to 3 clips on all three add paths:
- a focused library row;
- focus on the page body (the global Enter shortcut);
- the ＋ დამატება button.

This changes the user's arrangement and comes from the same cause as rounds 97–98, so it goes ahead of the cosmetic export-footer fixes.

**Round 99 task (`current-task.md`, decision D-29z64):**
- **Fix:** the add happens only on the first key press; auto-repeats add nothing. A gets three small edits:
  - `ArrangementLibrary.tsx` l.242–247 (the row's Enter);
  - `StudioWorkspace.tsx` l.1960–1968 (the global Enter);
  - `ArrangementLibraryPreview.tsx` l.304–311 (the ＋ button).
- **Frozen:** `ArrangementContext.tsx`, the export dialog, the toolbar and all protected and auth files.
- **Tests:** a new `held-enter-add.test.tsx` with 8 tests. A must show 4 of them failing on the old code (single add, fewer than three clips, one Undo step) and run mutations a–h.
- **Docs:** doc 086's status line, plus a new doc 087.
- **C checks in the browser, both viewports:** holding Enter on the row, on the page body and on ＋ adds exactly 1 clip.
- **C regression checks:** fresh presses and double-click still add, held arrow keys still move the selection, Space play/stop and the round 98 export fix still work, and a real WAV still exports. C also re-checks that no network or auth requests are made and that the source matches the baseline.
- **Expected end state:** 4 modified files and 2 new ones.

**Other planning changes:**
- **Status board:** SRW-12 (the library) is marked as having an open bug until round 99 passes. No item was promoted to მზადაა.
- **New backlog items:**
  - a test-helper duplication nit from the gate review;
  - an unprobed hypothesis that holding Enter on ▶ მოუსმინე toggles the preview on every repeat (B-R98-H1).
- **Architecture:** both reviewers said keep. I recorded their notes as addendum (k) to the checkpoint request: the repeat-Enter guard will be in 5 places after round 99, and the copied test setup is in 10 files. Nothing is scheduled and nothing blocks.
- **Advisor:** available; I used it twice and took its corrections to the test and browser-check wording.

**What's next:** the regression round is not due yet (last on 2026-10-21; it needs 3 days), so the next planning on or after 2026-10-24 will be the regression round. After that come the export-footer fixes, then the rest of the queue through T12 and VISUAL-A-OBSIDIAN.

**Why not COMPLETE or BLOCKED:**
- Still open:
  - SRW-12's bug;
  - the purchased-library mount work (SRW-21);
  - T12 and VISUAL-A-OBSIDIAN;
  - the remaining Low bugs;
  - the regression round;
  - the manual Tech Lead checks;
  - MP3 export in the production build.
- Only the purchased-library mount waits on someone else (the auth owner's release), so the loop isn't blocked.
